claims.text: Role in HPT: medically managed pts: osteoporosis is treated w bisphosphonates;
claims.quote: Osteoporosis is treated with bisphosphonates.

claims.text: for marked hypercalcemia: calcitonin (salmon) 4 to 8 IU/kg SC every 12 h; can ↓Ca by 1 to 2 mg/dL within a few hours.
claims.quote: A salmon calcitonin dosage of 4 to 8 IU/kg subcutaneously every 12 hours is safe. Calcitonin can lower serum calcium levels by 1 to 2 mg/dL within a few hours.

claims.text: Alendronate (Fosamax) dose, treatment of osteoporosis: Tx of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and in men: 10 mg daily or 70 mg (tablet or oral solution) once weekly.
claims.quote: Treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and in men: 10 mg daily or 70 mg (tablet or oral solution) once weekly.

claims.text: Swallow tablets whole w/ 6-8 ounces plain water at least 30 min b4 the first food, drink, or medication of the day.
claims.quote: Swallow tablets whole with 6-8 ounces plain water at least 30 minutes before the first food, drink, or medication of the day.

claims.text: ⍉ lie down for at least 30 min after taking and until after food.
claims.quote: Not lie down for at least 30 minutes after taking FOSAMAX and until after food.

claims.text: Alendronate (Fosamax) safety: CI: abnormalities of the esophagus which delay esophageal emptying such as stricture or achalasia.
claims.quote: Abnormalities of the esophagus which delay esophageal emptying such as stricture or achalasia

claims.text: CI: inability to stand or sit upright for at least 30 min.
claims.quote: Inability to stand or sit upright for at least 30 minutes

claims.text: CI: hypocalcemia.
claims.quote: Hypocalcemia (4, 5.2)

claims.text: Esophageal reactions (esophagitis, ulcers, erosions) reported; be alert for signs and instruct pts to discontinue and seek medical attention for dysphagia, odynophagia, retrosternal pain, or new/worsening heartburn.
claims.quote: Physicians should therefore be alert to any signs or symptoms signaling a possible esophageal reaction and patients should be instructed to discontinue FOSAMAX and seek medical attention if they develop dysphagia, odynophagia, retrosternal pain or new or worsening heartburn.

claims.text: Hypocalcemia must be corrected b4 initiating therapy.
claims.quote: Hypocalcemia must be corrected before initiating therapy with FOSAMAX

claims.text: Severe bone, joint, muscle pain may occur; discontinue use if severe symptoms develop.
claims.quote: Severe Bone, Joint, Muscle Pain may occur. Discontinue use if severe symptoms develop.

claims.text: ONJ reported (can occur spontaneously; generally associated w/ tooth extraction and/or local infection w/ delayed healing).
claims.quote: Osteonecrosis of the jaw (ONJ), which can occur spontaneously, is generally associated with tooth extraction and/or local infection with delayed healing, and has been reported in patients taking bisphosphonates, including FOSAMAX.

claims.text: Atypical fractures incl femoral fractures reported; pts w/ new thigh or groin pain should be evaluated to rule out a femoral fracture; re-evaluate risk/benefit and consider interrupting bisphosphonate therapy.
claims.quote: Atypical Fractures Including Femoral Fractures have been reported. Patients with new thigh or groin pain should be evaluated to rule out a femoral fracture. Risk/benefit of continuing bisphosphonate therapy should be re-evaluated in these patients and interruption of bisphosphonate therapy should be considered

claims.text: Not recommended if CrCl less than 35 mL/min.
claims.quote: FOSAMAX is not recommended for patients with creatinine clearance less than 35 mL/min.

claims.text: Calcium, antacids, or oral medications containing multivalent cations interfere w/ absorption; instruct pts to wait at least one-half hour after FOSAMAX b4 any other oral medication.
claims.quote: Co-administration of FOSAMAX and calcium, antacids, or oral medications containing multivalent cations will interfere with absorption of FOSAMAX. Therefore, instruct patients to wait at least one-half hour after taking FOSAMAX before taking any other oral medications.

claims.text: OD: hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and upper GI adverse events may result; give milk or antacids to bind alendronate; ⍉ induce vomiting (risk of esophageal irritation); keep the pt fully upright.
claims.quote: Hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia, and upper gastrointestinal adverse events, such as upset stomach, heartburn, esophagitis, gastritis, or ulcer, may result from oral overdosage. Milk or antacids should be given to bind alendronate. Due to the risk of esophageal irritation, vomiting should not be induced and the patient should remain fully upright.

claims.text: Calcitonin salmon (Miacalcin) safety: CI: hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon or any of the excipients (reactions incl anaphylaxis w/ death, bronchospasm, and swelling of the tongue or throat).
claims.quote: Hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon or any of the excipients. Reactions have included anaphylaxis with death, bronchospasm, and swelling of the tongue or throat

claims.text: Serious hypersensitivity reactions incl fatal anaphylaxis reported; consider skin testing b4 treatment in pts w/ suspected hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon.
claims.quote: Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including reports of fatal anaphylaxis have been reported. Consider skin testing prior to treatment in patients with suspected hypersensitivity to calcitonin salmon

claims.text: Hypocalcemia w/ tetany (muscle cramps, twitching) and seizure activity reported; hypocalcemia must be corrected b4 initiating therapy.
claims.quote: Hypocalcemia associated with tetany (i.e., muscle cramps, twitching) and seizure activity has been reported with Miacalcin injection therapy. Hypocalcemia must be corrected before initiating therapy.

claims.text: Meta-analysis of 21 trials suggests an ↑ risk of overall malignancies in calcitonin salmon-treated pts.
claims.quote: A meta-analysis of 21 clinical trials suggests an increased risk of overall malignancies in calcitonin salmon-treated patients

claims.text: Circulating antibodies to calcitonin salmon may develop and may cause loss of response to treatment.
claims.quote: Circulating antibodies to calcitonin salmon may develop, and may cause loss of response to treatment

claims.text: Use for Paget's dz or postmenopausal osteoporosis is recommended w/ an adequate intake of Ca and vitamin D.
claims.quote: Use of Miacalcin injection for the treatment of Paget’s disease or postmenopausal osteoporosis is recommended in conjunction with an adequate intake of calcium and vitamin D

claims.text: Concomitant lithium may ↓ plasma lithium concentrations (↑ urinary clearance); lithium dose may require adjustment.
claims.quote: Concomitant use of calcitonin salmon and lithium may lead to a reduction in plasma lithium concentrations due to increased urinary clearance of lithium. The dose of lithium may require adjustment.

claims.text: OD: hypocalcemic tetany could occur; keep parenteral calcium available for treatment.
claims.quote: The pharmacologic actions of Miacalcin injection suggest that hypocalcemic tetany could occur in overdose. Therefore, provisions for parenteral administration of calcium should be available for the treatment of overdose.

claims.text: Most common adverse reactions: nausea w/ or w/o vomiting (10%), injection site inflammation (10%), and flushing of the face or hands (2% to 5%).
claims.quote: Most common adverse reactions are nausea with or without vomiting (10%), injection site inflammation (10%), and flushing of the face or hands (2% to 5%)

claims.text: Due to the possible association between malignancy and calcitonin salmon use, the need for continued therapy should be re-evaluated periodically.
claims.quote: Due to the possible association between malignancy and calcitonin salmon use, the need for continued therapy should be re-evaluated on a periodic basis
